jp: 飼育当番[しいくとうばん]の私[わたし]は、毎朝[まいあさ]ウサギにえさを{やります|gv-yaru}。
en: As the animal-care monitor, I feed the rabbits every morning.
why: I am the giver and the rabbits are animals, so やる is the verb; くれる would need someone giving to me.

jp: 学校[がっこう]の花壇[かだん]の花[はな]に、放課後[ほうかご]水[みず]を{やります|gv-yaru}。
en: After school I water the flowers in the school flower bed.
why: Giving water to plants is the classic use of やる; the other verbs change who gives and who receives.

jp: 生物部[せいぶつぶ]の私[わたし]は、毎日[まいにち]カメにえさを{やっています|gv-yaru}。
en: As a member of the biology club, I feed the turtle every day.
why: I give food to an animal, so やる; くれる and さしあげる need a person receiving, and もらう reverses the direction.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]の観葉植物[かんようしょくぶつ]に、週[しゅう]に二回[にかい]水[みず]を{やります|gv-yaru}。
en: I water the office's potted plants twice a week.
why: The receiver is a plant, so the speaker uses やる for giving it water.

jp: 研究室[けんきゅうしつ]のマウスに、毎朝[まいあさ]決[き]まった量[りょう]のえさを{やりました|gv-yaru}。
en: Every morning I gave the lab mice a fixed amount of food.
why: Feeding laboratory animals is giving to creatures below the giver, which calls for やる.

jp: 農業[のうぎょう]高校[こうこう]の生徒[せいと]たちは、牛[うし]に干[ほ]し草[くさ]を{やります|gv-yaru}。
en: The students at the agricultural high school give hay to the cows.
why: Students give hay to cattle: a giver feeding animals uses やる, not the receiving verbs もらう and いただく.

jp: 部活[ぶかつ]の後輩[こうはい]に、お昼[ひる]のパンを{やりました|gv-yaru}。
en: I gave my junior club member my lunch bread.
why: A senior giving to a junior uses やる; さしあげる is for superiors, and くれる and もらう change the direction.

jp: 弟[おとうと]に使[つか]い古[ふる]した辞書[じしょ]を{やりました|gv-yaru}。
en: I gave my younger brother my well-worn dictionary.
why: The giver is me and the receiver is my younger brother, a junior, so やる fits; さしあげる would be far too humble.

jp: 妹[いもうと]には、試験[しけん]に合格[ごうかく]したらノートパソコンを{やる|gv-yaru}つもりです。
en: I plan to give my younger sister a laptop if she passes the exam.
why: I will give to my younger sister, so やる; もらう would mean I receive the laptop from her.

jp: 後輩[こうはい]に、がんばったごほうびのジュースを{やった|gv-yaru}。
en: I gave my junior a juice as a reward for working hard.
why: A senior gives a reward to a junior with やる; くれる and もらう reverse the flow, and いただく is humble.

jp: 教室[きょうしつ]の金魚[きんぎょ]にえさを{やる|gv-yaru}のは、毎日[まいにち]私[わたし]の仕事[しごと]です。
en: Feeding the goldfish in the classroom is my job every day.
why: The one who feeds the goldfish is the giver, and animals take やる.

jp: 出張[しゅっちょう]の間[あいだ]、同僚[どうりょう]が鉢植[はちう]えに水[みず]を{やって|gv-yaru}くれました。
en: While I was away on a business trip, a colleague watered my potted plants.
why: The colleague gives water to plants, so the main verb is やる (て-form), followed by くれました for the favour to me.

jp: 昼休[ひるやす]みに、中庭[なかにわ]の池[いけ]の鯉[こい]にパンくずを{やっていました|gv-yaru}。
en: During the lunch break I was feeding bread crumbs to the carp in the courtyard pond.
why: Feeding fish is giving to animals, which takes やる; the other verbs do not fit a giver and an animal.

jp: 新入社員[しんにゅうしゃいん]に、ぼくの古[ふる]い名刺入[めいしい]れを{やりました|gv-yaru}。
en: I gave the new employee my old business-card case.
why: A senior colleague gives something to a newcomer below him, which is やる; もらう would reverse who receives.

jp: 夏休[なつやす]みの間[あいだ]、学校[がっこう]の花[はな]に水[みず]を{やる|gv-yaru}当番[とうばん]が回[まわ]ってきます。
en: During the summer holidays, the duty of watering the school's flowers comes round to each of us.
why: Watering the flowers is giving water to plants, so the duty is described with やる.

jp: 校庭[こうてい]の木[き]に、先生[せんせい]と一緒[いっしょ]に肥料[ひりょう]を{やりました|gv-yaru}。
en: Together with the teacher, I gave fertiliser to the trees in the school grounds.
why: The receiver is a tree, so the giver (us) uses やる; さしあげる is only for people above you.

jp: 弟[おとうと]が飼[か]っているハムスターに、私[わたし]が代[か]わりにえさを{やりました|gv-yaru}。
en: I fed my brother's hamster in his place.
why: I am the giver and the receiver is a hamster, so やる; もらう and いただく would make me the receiver.

jp: 私[わたし]たちが水[みず]を{やらない|gv-yaru}と、教室[きょうしつ]のひまわりが枯[か]れてしまいます。
en: If we don't water them, the sunflowers in the classroom will wither.
why: Not giving water to plants is やらない; くれない would mean no one gives to me, which does not fit.

jp: 実験[じっけん]用[よう]の稲[いね]に、決[き]まった時間[じかん]に栄養液[えいようえき]を{やります|gv-yaru}。
en: I give the experimental rice plants a nutrient solution at fixed times.
why: Giving nutrients to plants is やる; もらう would reverse the roles, and くれる and さしあげる need a person as receiver.

jp: 同期[どうき]の田中[たなか]さんは、毎朝[まいあさ]会社[かいしゃ]のサボテンに水[みず]を{やっています|gv-yaru}。
en: My fellow new hire Mr. Tanaka waters the office cactus every morning.
why: A colleague's giving water to a plant is やる; くれる needs a person giving to the speaker.

jp: 大学[だいがく]の実習[じっしゅう]で、子牛[こうし]にミルクを{やりました|gv-yaru}。
en: In a university practical, I gave milk to a calf.
why: The receiver is a calf, an animal, so the giver uses やる.

jp: 試験[しけん]の前[まえ]の日[ひ]、後輩[こうはい]にお守[まも]りを{やりました|gv-yaru}。
en: The day before the exam, I gave my junior a good-luck charm.
why: A senior gives a charm to a junior: やる; もらう would mean the junior gave it to me.

jp: 学校[がっこう]で飼[か]っているウサギにキャベツを{やって|gv-yaru}もいいですか。
en: May I give some cabbage to the rabbits we keep at school?
why: The speaker asks permission to give cabbage to animals, so the て-form of やる is needed.

jp: 夜[よる]は、植木[うえき]に水[みず]を{やらない|gv-yaru}ほうがいいと、先生[せんせい]に教[おし]えてもらいました。
en: The teacher told me that it's better not to water the plants at night.
why: The advice is about not giving water to plants, so やらない; the other verbs change who gives and receives.

jp: 職員室[しょくいんしつ]の水槽[すいそう]の魚[さかな]に、帰[かえ]る前[まえ]にえさを{やります|gv-yaru}。
en: Before going home I feed the fish in the staff room tank.
why: Fish are animals the speaker gives food to, so やる.

jp: 仕事[しごと]から帰[かえ]ってすぐ、家庭[かてい]菜園[さいえん]のトマトに水[みず]を{やります|gv-yaru}。
en: As soon as I get home from work, I water the tomatoes in my vegetable garden.
why: Plants receive water from the speaker, which is やる; いただく would make the speaker the receiver.

jp: 卒業[そつぎょう]する時[とき]、後輩[こうはい]に参考書[さんこうしょ]を全部[ぜんぶ]{やりました|gv-yaru}。
en: When I graduated, I gave all my reference books to my juniors.
why: A graduating senior gives books to juniors with やる; さしあげる is for people above you.

jp: 学校[がっこう]の池[いけ]のカモにパンを{やらない|gv-yaru}でくださいと、書[か]いてあります。
en: A sign says, "Please do not feed bread to the ducks in the school pond."
why: The ban is on people giving bread to animals, so やらないで; the other verbs do not fit giving to ducks.

jp: 会社[かいしゃ]の屋上[おくじょう]の菜園[さいえん]で、野菜[やさい]に水[みず]を{やっている|gv-yaru}のは総務部[そうむぶ]の人[ひと]です。
en: The people watering the vegetables in the rooftop garden of the company are from the general affairs department.
why: Watering vegetables means giving to plants, so やっている; the other verbs change the direction or the level.

jp: 出張[しゅっちょう]中[ちゅう]、うちの猫[ねこ]に毎日[まいにち]えさを{やって|gv-yaru}ほしいと、隣[となり]の人[ひと]にお願[ねが]いしました。
en: I asked my neighbour to feed my cat every day while I was away on business.
why: The neighbour is asked to give food to the cat, so やって; くれて and もらって do not fit a request to feed an animal.

jp: 小学校[しょうがっこう]の先生[せんせい]は、花[はな]に水[みず]を{やる|gv-yaru}係[かかり]を決[き]めました。
en: The primary school teacher decided on a person to be in charge of watering the flowers.
why: The job is giving water to flowers, so the noun-modifying form やる is used.
